subtype: Child seeking cuddles after a bad day [Actor]
passage:
In the clinic waiting room, Asif, five, came out of the injection room with red eyes. The nurse had said, "Big boys don't make such a fuss."
Without a word, he climbed into Ammi's lap and pressed his face into her dupatta.
Nazia didn't ask questions. She wrapped both arms around him and rocked a little.
After a while Asif mumbled, "It hurt. And she said I was a baby."
"It did hurt. And you were scared. That's allowed," Nazia said, stroking his hair.

qa.q: What did Asif press his face into?
qa.a: He pressed his face into Ammi's dupatta.

qa.q: How was Asif feeling when he climbed into Ammi's lap?
qa.a: He was hurt, scared and a little ashamed after the injection and the nurse's comment.

qa.q: What did Nazia do well that others could learn from?
qa.a: She held him first without questions and only talked once he was ready, naming that being scared was allowed.

qa.q: What might Nazia have felt seeing Asif come out with red eyes?
qa.a: She probably felt a pang of sympathy and wanted to comfort him, so she simply held him.

grounding: It shows a young child who climbs silently into a lap after a scary moment, and a mother who hugs first and talks later.

subtype: Child seeking cuddles after a bad day [Actor]
passage:
I'm Gautam, from upstairs. I was dropping off a parcel when I saw it.
Zainab, who is five, had just been scolded by her Ammi for spilling a jar of pickle. She didn't cry, but her face went tight. She walked slowly to her Abbu on the sofa and, without a word, climbed into his lap.
He put his paper down and just held her. He didn't ask anything. After a while she whispered in his ear, and he said, "Let's go help Ammi clean up."
I can't say what she felt, but she hopped down looking lighter.

qa.q: What had Zainab spilled on the floor?
qa.a: She had spilled a jar of pickle.

qa.q: What might Zainab have been feeling when she walked slowly to the sofa?
qa.a: She may have felt upset and ashamed after being scolded, though Gautam can't be sure.

qa.q: What did Zainab's Abbu do that helped?
qa.a: He put the paper down and held her first without asking questions, and then helped her make it right.

qa.q: How might Zainab's Ammi feel when they come to help clean up?
qa.a: She would probably feel calmer and glad to see Zainab trying to fix the spill.

grounding: It shows, through a neighbour's eyes, a young child who climbs silently into a lap after being scolded, and a father who holds her first and talks later.
